chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ibn Rabat, from Sayf al-Tammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever looks at the Ka'bah, a good deed is written for him and a bad deed is erased from him, until he turns his gaze away from it.

key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: The Ka'bah, the cubic building in Mecca

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for looking at the Ka'bah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the Ka'bah as a focal point for divine mercy, where sustained visual contemplation yields continuous spiritual purification. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on the Ka'bah not merely as a directional marker for prayer, but as a tangible symbol of God's presence that facilitates the erasure of sins through mindful gaze.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Ibn Rabat, from Sayf Al Tammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who looks at the Kabah, the writing of the Rewards for him and the deletion of sins would not cease from it, until he turns his eyesight away from it’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub from al-Hassan ibn Ali from ibn Ribat from Sayf al- Tammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
as long as one keeps looking at al-Ka’bah, one good deed is written for him and one bad deed is deleted until he turns away from looking at al-Ka’bah.”
